messages:
sre-oncall: getting multiple customer reports of 502/504s from hosted-api (eu1) starting ~11:02 UTC. spike in errors and latency. sample trace: 01GZ8Y2X-abc123. attaching curl that reproduces 502 locally. anyone oncall able to triage?

amy_support: confirmed — ticket ACME-789 opened by Acme Inc. They see 502 on streaming responses and on short sync requests too. customer pasted response headers: 
HTTP/2 502
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: 01GZ8Y2X-abc123

They say it started right after a large embed batch from their tenant. :frowny:

jon_eng: looking at edge dashboards — envoy upstream_connect_fails and upstream_reset are spiking across a subset of frontdoors. midproxy shows a flurry of HTTP/2 GOAWAYs at 11:01-11:04. initial suspicion: upstream auth or billing proxy flapping, causing edge to send 502 back. grep from one midproxy log: 

[2025-06-12T11:02:04.321Z] envoy upstream reset before response: connection reset by peer, error_code=\"CONNECT_ERROR\"

Also seeing `upstream response timeout` in a few nginx instances.

maria_sre: can you paste a minimal repro curl? Also which backend route is the failing path (generation vs embeddings)?

sre-oncall: here's the curl that reproduces a quick 502 from eu1: 

```bash
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED\" \\
  -H \"X-Model-Name: redwood/gpt-4-mini\" \\
  -d '{\"input\":\"hi\"}' \\
  https://api.eu1.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

response: 

> HTTP/2 502
> server: envoy
> date: Fri, 12 Jun 2025 11:02:05 GMT
> content-length: 98
> 
>{"error":{"message":"Upstream service unavailable","code":502}}

amy_support: customer also reported one POST that actually returned 200 then a subsequent streaming call returned 502 mid-stream. They say their request pattern was a burst of ~2000 small embed calls over 30s.

jon_eng: that pattern could exhaust keepalive/connection pools on upstream auth or tenant router. I’m checking pod metrics for auth-proxy on eu1: 

```
kubectl get hpa -n infra auth-proxy-eu1
NAME               REFERENCE             TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
auth-proxy-eu1     Deployment/auth-proxy 75%/80%       2         10        8
```

kubectl logs auth-proxy-7f9 | tail -n 50 | grep -i \"connection reset\"

-> a lot of `connection reset by peer` and `accept queue full` messages starting 11:01.

maria_sre: can we temporarily route tenants hitting embed-heavy endpoints to a fallback pool or increase upstream keepalive pools? We should also check if nginx/envoy connection window sizes are being exhausted by many short lived streams.

sre-oncall: trying two mitigations now: 1) scale auth-proxy to +50% replicas and 2) bump envoy upstream keepalive connections from 100 -> 250 on the affected frontdoors. Will monitor.

deploy-bot: manual scaling action recorded: svc/autoscaler increased auth-proxy-eu1 replicas from 8 -> 12 at 11:06:02 UTC by @sre-oncall.

jon_eng: I ran a quick probe after scaling: upstream_connect_fails dropped by ~65% in the 11:09-11:12 window. early signs look good. still seeing a few stray 502s tied to tenant stream churn.

customer-success: Acme Inc is on the call and appreciates the quick response. They asked for repro steps so they can test after we finish. Here's a short reproducible script we gave them: 

```bash
for i in {1..300}; do \\
  curl -s -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED\" -d '{\"input\":\"embed me\"}' https://api.eu1.redwood.example/v1/embeddings &\\
  sleep 0.05;
done
wait
```

They say the stream that 502s is the one that lands in the middle of that loop.

maria_sre: please capture conntrack and netstat on the auth-proxy node if you can. also capture envoy stats: `envoy_admin?stats` filtered by upstream_cx_* and upstream_reset_* for the timeframe.

amy_support: collecting traces and attaching to ticket. I put the sample trace id and curl into the ticket and included the mitigation steps we took. Will notify the customer to retry after ~11:18 UTC. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: update: after scaling and keepalive bump, 502 rate dropped to baseline by 11:15 UTC. monitoring shows residual 504s on long-lived streams only (likely client-side timeouts while we reopened pools).

jon_eng: assigning follow-up to eng-runtime to investigate root cause: suspected connection pool exhaustion + h2 stream window interactions under bursts of small embed requests. Recommend we: 
- reproduce locally with concurrent embed bursts
- run histograms of idle conn reuse and socket churn
- evaluate config: upstream idle_timeout, max_conns, h2_max_concurrent_streams

sre-oncall: leaving this thread open for 30m to validate stability. if error rate doesn't creep back up we'll close and create an RFC for connection pool hardening. cc @maria_sre @jon_eng @amy_support :eyes:

customer-success: customer confirmed retry after 11:20 — they see successful requests and said errors largely resolved. thanked team.

amy_support: will add postmortem notes to ticket and schedule follow-up with Acme to review rate limiting/batching best practices.

maria_sre: :thumbsup: will start a short runbook item for future bursts (scale plan + quick config tweaks).

sre-oncall: closing mitigation checklist: scaled auth-proxy, bumped keepalive, monitored envoys -> decreased 502s. root cause investigation assigned to eng-runtime. thread will be linked from the incident log.
